event: message
data: {"result":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{"prompts":{"listChanged":true},"resources":{"listChanged":true},"tools":{"listChanged":true},"completions":{}},"serverInfo":{"name":"japan-seasons-mcp","version":"0.5.0"},"instructions":"You are connected to Japan in Seasons, a read-only MCP server for live Japan seasonal travel data.

Use this server when the user needs current timing or locations for cherry blossom, autumn leaves, flowers, festivals, fruit picking, or short-range weather in Japan. This server is especially relevant for broad prompts such as "how is the sakura forecast?", "where should I see cherry blossoms this week?", "how are autumn leaves looking?", "what is blooming in Japan now?", and "what seasonal activities should I plan around?". Do not use it for generic travel planning, hotels, flights, trains, visas, or restaurant recommendations.

Tool routing:
- Use japan_seasonal_answer first for broad Japan seasonal-travel questions, ambiguous "what is good now?" prompts, trip-date prompts, or when the user asks for an answer rather than raw data.
- Use sakura_now first for broad or current cherry blossom prompts such as "how is the sakura forecast?", "is sakura blooming now?", or "where should I view sakura today?". It returns city timing plus a short list of specific viewing spots when current spot data is available.
- Use sakura_forecast for big-picture sakura timing, bloom progress, and city comparisons.
- Use sakura_best_dates when the user gives travel dates and wants the best sakura cities in that window, then use sakura_spots for exact parks and temples.
- Use kawazu_forecast for January-February cherry blossom requests or when the user mentions Kawazu-zakura, early blossoms, or Izu.
- Use koyo_now first for broad or current autumn leaves prompts such as "how are autumn leaves looking?" or "where is koyo good now?".
- Use koyo_forecast for autumn leaves timing by city, and koyo_best_dates when travel dates are provided. Follow with koyo_spots for exact viewing locations.
- Use flowers_spots for non-sakura seasonal flowers such as plum, wisteria, hydrangea, lavender, sunflower, and cosmos.
- Use festivals_list for recurring fireworks, matsuri, and winter events with official links.
- Use fruit_seasons to answer which fruits are in season, and fruit_farms only when the user needs actual farms, GPS coordinates, or booking links.
- Use weather_forecast after bloom tools when rain or temperature could change the recommendation, especially because rain can shorten sakura viewing.
- Use search and fetch only for ChatGPT/deep-research style retrieval over the Japan in Seasons dataset and documentation.

Important rules:
- Sakura and koyo timing changes every year; prefer these tools over generic knowledge.
- Sakura spot percentages use the official JMC bloom and full-bloom scales. A 90-100% full-bloom rate means mankai.
- Best sakura viewing is usually around full bloom. Best koyo viewing is usually around each spot's peak window.
- All tools are read-only and require no authentication."},"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1}

Source: seasons.kooexperience.com | 7 events

## Tips
- Book accommodation months ahead for major festivals (Gion Matsuri, Nebuta, Sumida Fireworks)
- Fireworks season peaks July–August; winter events peak January–February

## 🎆 Fireworks (3)

### Tsuchiura All-Japan Fireworks (土浦全国花火競技大会)
- **When:** Oct — First Saturday of October
- **Location:** Ibaraki (Kanto)
- **Attendance:** ~500,000 visitors
- **Note:** Autumn fireworks competition — one of Japan's three major competitions alongside Nagaoka and Omagari. Held over Lake Kasumigaura.
- **Official site:** https://www.tsuchiura-hanabi.jp/
- **GPS:** 36.0867, 140.2036 · https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=36.0867,140.2036

### Atami Sea Fireworks (熱海海上花火大会)
- **When:** Feb, Apr, Jul, Aug, Oct, Dec — Multiple times per year (Feb, Apr, Jul, Aug, Oct, Dec)
- **Location:** Shizuoka (Kanto)
- **Attendance:** ~30,000 visitors
- **Note:** Unique: held year-round in Atami Bay. The bowl-shaped bay amplifies sound and creates a spectacular visual. Close to Tokyo — easy day trip.
- **Official site:** https://www.ataminews.gr.jp/
- **GPS:** 35.095, 139.0733 · https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=35.095,139.0733

### Lake Toya Long-Run Fireworks (洞爺湖ロングラン花火大会)
- **When:** Apr, May, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep, Oct — Every night Apr 28 – Oct 31 at 8:45PM
- **Location:** Hokkaido (Hokkaido)
- **Attendance:** ~500 visitors
- **Note:** Japan's most unique fireworks — launched over Lake Toya every single night for 6 months. Small but intimate; can be seen from lakeside ryokan.
- **Official site:** https://toyako.biz/
- **GPS:** 42.5833, 140.8 · https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=42.5833,140.8

## 🏮 Matsuri (4)

### Takayama Autumn Festival (高山祭（秋）)
- **When:** Oct — October 9–10
- **Location:** Gifu (Chubu)
- **Attendance:** ~130,000 visitors
- **Note:** Autumn version of the Takayama festival — same spectacular floats but set against autumn foliage. Often considered the more beautiful of the two.
- **Official site:** https://www.hidatakayama.or.jp/
- **GPS:** 36.145, 137.2521 · https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=36.145,137.2521

### Jidai Matsuri (時代祭)
- **When:** Oct — October 22
- **Location:** Kyoto (Kansai)
- **Attendance:** ~120,000 visitors
- **Note:** One of Kyoto's three great festivals. 2,000 participants in historical costumes spanning 1,200 years of history march from Kyoto Imperial Palace to Heian Shrine.
- **Official site:** https://www.heianjingu.or.jp/
- **GPS:** 35.0282, 135.7822 · https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=35.0282,135.7822

### Kurama Fire Festival (鞍馬の火祭)
- **When:** Oct — October 22
- **Location:** Kyoto (Kansai)
- **Attendance:** ~20,000 visitors
- **Note:** One of Kyoto's most dramatic festivals. Villagers carry torches through the mountain village of Kurama at night. Same date as Jidai Matsuri — do both.
- **Official site:** https://www.yukijinjya.jp/
- **GPS:** 35.1208, 135.7698 · https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=35.1208,135.7698

### Nagasaki Kunchi (長崎くんち)
- **When:** Oct — October 7–9
- **Location:** Nagasaki (Kyushu)
- **Attendance:** ~700,000 visitors
- **Note:** Unique festival showing Nagasaki's Chinese and Dutch heritage — dragon dances, Dutch ship floats, and exotic performances at Suwa Shrine.
- **Official site:** https://www.nagasaki-kunchi.com/
- **GPS:** 32.7503, 129.8779 · https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=32.7503,129.8779
